description: Unit: a contact-scoped visibility context with no profile grants produces exactly today's own-tickets predicate.
Unit: a contact-scoped context with grants matches own tickets, tickets on a granted profile, and NULL-profile tickets when the client default profile is granted — and nothing else.
Unit: client scope and the client-admin override ignore profile grants entirely.
Unit: applyTicketVisibilityFilter without a billingProfileColumn is byte-identical to the pre-existing behaviour even when grants are present, so an un-migrated call site cannot widen visibility.
Unit: getClientContactVisibilityContext loads only grants whose profile belongs to the contact's own client and only rows with can_view_profile_tickets.
Unit: the merge guard matrix rejects same-client merges, an already-merged source or target, a missing client, and a soft parent-link cycle.
Unit: the merge plan moves every source profile, renames the source default to the client name, clears is_default/is_system_managed_default, and keeps every billing_profile_id.
Unit: work items arriving with a NULL billing_profile_id are stamped with the source's moved default profile, and work items already carrying a profile are left alone.
Unit: contract cutover produces a terminated source contract plus a clone on the target starting at the cutover date; original-date moves leave the dates untouched.

Behaviour: a full merge round trip moves profiles, invoices, cycles, payment methods, tickets, contacts, visibility groups and inbound domains, writes an audit row, publishes CLIENT_MERGED and leaves the source archived with one fresh system-managed default profile.
note: server/src/test/integration/clientMerge.integration.test.ts drives the merge through the server action against a real database (profiles, invoices, cycles, tickets, contacts, groups, inbound domains, audit row, CLIENT_MERGED, fresh default on the shell, re-merge refused), including invoices/transactions/credit_tracking rows that arrive with no billing profile. packages/clients/src/lib/clientMergeEngine.test.ts covers the same orchestration against an in-memory database.

description: Integration: the parent's billing output is identical before and after a merge, and a moved billing cycle regenerates an identical invoice.
note: server/src/test/integration/clientMerge.integration.test.ts: the parent's finalized invoice projection (totals, per-line amounts, tax, credit) is byte-identical after a merge, and the absorbed client's moved February cycle regenerates the money projection its pre-merge January cycle produced, with every charge still attributed to the moved profile rather than the parent's default. This test is what surfaced M033: without re-pointing contracts.owner_client_id the regeneration fails outright with 'Recurring service periods were not materialized for this recurring execution window'.

description: Integration: a granted profile manager sees the profile's tickets before and after the merge; an ungranted contact sees only their own.
note: server/src/test/integration/clientMerge.integration.test.ts asserts the pre/post-merge portal round trip against a real database through getClientContactVisibilityContext + applyTicketVisibilityFilter: the granted manager sees own + profile tickets and not the parent's, the ungranted colleague sees only their own. The predicate shapes are additionally unit-tested in packages/tickets/src/lib/clientPortalVisibility.test.ts.

description: Behaviour: grant pinning writes explicit client_portal_user_billing_profiles rows for previously unrestricted source portal users and leaves already-restricted users alone.
note: Behaviour: grant pinning writes rows for unrestricted portal users and writes none when switched off.

description: Behaviour: re-merging an already merged source is refused.
note: Behaviour: a second merge of the same source raises ClientMergeBlockedError.

description: Contract: the merge, preview and profile-contact endpoints are registered in OpenAPI with real metadata and surface in the generated MCP registry.

Integration: merging two clients that each have a logo succeeds; the target keeps its own logo, the absorbed one arrives demoted to a plain document, and a variant the target does not use is inherited.
note: server/src/test/integration/clientMerge.integration.test.ts seeds an is_entity_logo association on both clients against a real database. Without the fix it reproduces the operator's failure verbatim: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_document_associations_single_true_logo". The three slot outcomes (taken, free, shared document) are unit-tested in packages/clients/src/lib/clientMergeEngine.test.ts.
